objective: Package the Mesa 26.0.8 Teflon/VIP9000 source changes, which currently exist only as a patched source tree on the proxmox build host and as a prebuilt libteflon.so in the orangepi4A repo, into a small, reviewable source patch bundle. Publish the bundle inside NPU_modules_opi4a_6.18.44 and validate that the patch reproduces the shipped libteflon.so and that the rebuilt delegate still runs the Allwinner T527 VIP9000 NPU on the Orange Pi 4A.

not_committed: Full Mesa 26.0.8 source tree (~200 MB) - unnecessary and too large for GitHub
Build directories, object files, ninja logs
*.bak and __pycache__ files from the patched tree

change_themes: VIP9000 multi-core (multi-VIP) sync/stall emission gated behind ETNA_ENABLE_STALL
VIP9000 init_npu() register programming (NN/TP debug, USC control, icache, SRAM remap)
Skip 3D transposes and 3D-only registers for non-3D tensors (model 0x9000)
Kernel-facing NPU detection/softpin fixes in etnaviv_screen.c and etnaviv_drm_winsys.c
Allwinner T527 VIP9000 HWDB entry (ChipID 0x9000, ProductID 0x5090009) and HWDB lookup fallbacks
Teflon tfl_device.c reshape handling and error-path hardening

Experimental env overrides: ETNA_ENABLE_STALL, ETNA_NN_TOKEN, ETNA_NN_CORES, ETNA_NN_CONFIG, ETNA_NN_LAYER_TYPE, ETNA_NN_NO_Z_OFFSET, ETNA_NN_LAYER_FLUSH, ETNA_NN_NO_FLUSH, ETNA_NN_SUPERBLOCKS, ETNA_NN_SRAM_CACHE, ETNA_NN_10A4, ETNA_NN_10A8, ETNA_MAX_OPS, ETNA_START_OP, ETNA_ALWAYS_INIT

patch_generation.method: temporary git repository on proxmox: extract pristine tarball, git init/commit baseline, overlay modified tree excluding build artifacts, then git diff --cached
verification: git diff --cached --stat matches the 10-file change set

build_reproduction.command: meson setup build <options> && ninja -C build src/gallium/targets/teflon/libteflon.so

level_1_patch_integrity: Extract pristine mesa_26.0.8.orig.tar.xz to a clean directory
Apply patch; confirm exit 0 and git apply --check passes
Confirm resulting tree byte-matches /root/builds/mesa-26.0.8 for the 10 changed files
level_2_binary_reproduction: Cross-rebuild libteflon.so from pristine+patch on proxmox
Match the original environment: non-git source tree (empty MESA_GIT_SHA1) and no libudev detection
Result: byte-for-byte identical to the shipped lib/libteflon.so (sha256 10bd3eae...)
The only nondeterminism is the ordering inside Mesa's generated src/etnaviv/isa/encode.h; reusing the original generated header yields the identical binary
level_3_functional_on_orange_pi: Ensure NPU driver enabled (NPU_enable.sh / etnaviv on /dev/dri/renderD129)
Run smoke_test/test_npu_smoke.py with repo libteflon.so and capture result
Install rebuilt libteflon.so to /usr/local/lib (with backup), run smoke test again
Compare pass/fail, initialization time, and inference result; restore original lib
level_4_native_rebuild_optional: Install libdrm-dev and any missing build deps on the Orange Pi 4A
Native meson/ninja build of the Teflon target (limit parallelism to avoid OOM)
Run smoke test with the natively built delegate
acceptance_criteria: Patch applies cleanly to pristine Mesa 26.0.8
Rebuilt delegate loads and executes conv2d.tflite on VIP9000
Smoke test result matches the shipped artifact
No regression in the published kernel/driver stack

risks: Byte-identical reproduction was achieved, but only after matching two environment details (empty MESA_GIT_SHA1, no libudev) and reusing the original generated encode.h; a fresh build with a random Python hash seed can reorder that generated header.
The Orange Pi 4A has 3.7 GB RAM and ~1.5 GB free; native Mesa builds can OOM. Use -j2/-j4 or rely on the proxmox cross-build.
Several changes are experimental and env-var gated; upstream reviewers may want them split into separate patches.
The repo lib/libteflon.so is unstripped; /root/builds/teflon_opi4a/libteflon.so is an older stripped artifact. Compare against the repo artifact, not the old stripped one.

repo_and_commit.decision: Yes - commit the patch bundle (small, reviewable) to NPU_modules_opi4a_6.18.44/mesa_patches; do NOT commit full Mesa source.

open_questions: Should the kernel-side etnaviv patches also be regenerated as patches against Linux 6.18.44 and added to the bundle?
Should the experimental env-gated changes be split into separate reviewable commits for the upstream Mesa MR?
